gold_rationale: Permanent, irreversible in vivo CRISPR knockout of SNCA via broadly biodistributed, constitutively expressed Cas9 is unsafe and not ready: alpha-synuclein has essential synaptic functions, so permanent loss risks irreversible harm; there is no unbiased off-target/genotoxicity analysis (double-strand breaks, large deletions, translocations); long-term Cas9 expression adds anti-Cas9 immunity and ongoing genotoxic exposure; and a permanent genomic edit cannot be titrated or reversed. 'Alpha-synuclein causes PD, so deleting it is curative' is an overclaim. The correct decision is No-Go; a safer approach uses regulatable/tunable, regionally restricted, aggregate- or allele-selective lowering (not permanent knockout) with thorough off-target characterization and patient stratification.
required_concepts: off-target editing / genotoxicity (no unbiased off-target analysis)
irreversibility (cannot titrate or reverse a genomic edit)
broad biodistribution / lack of cell-type restriction
'deleting alpha-synuclein is curative' is an overclaim
safer approach: regulatable, regionally restricted, selective lowering
red_flags: issues a Go for permanent, irreversible in vivo SNCA knockout
assumes deleting alpha-synuclein is curative / automatically safe
ignores essential physiological role of alpha-synuclein
ignores off-target editing / genotoxicity or the absence of off-target analysis
ignores long-term Cas9 immunity/genotoxicity or the irreversibility of a genomic edit
